ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. text:
Plant-parasitic nematodes affecting corn roots, including Heterodera zeae, Pratylenchus subranjani, and Meloidogyne hapla.

Symptoms: affected root systems show stunting, poor growth, yellowing, and wilting, particularly during hot or dry periods; depending on the species, roots may show galls (root-knot type) or lesions/necrosis. Symptoms often appear patchy across a field and are more commonly associated with sandy soil areas.

Management: crop rotation with non-host crops is the main management strategy, since nematodes can persist in soil for a long time and continuous corn cultivation allows populations to build up. Where nematode damage is suspected, soil sampling/testing can help confirm the problem. Nematicides exist but are not commonly used for corn in the Cambodian context described here, and resistant/tolerant corn varieties are limited.
